To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated a hierarchical simulation framework that is capable of predictive simulations of materials at the first-principles level and at the scale of billions of atoms, and that it is portable to high-end parallel supercomputer systems such as IBM Blue Gene/L and SGI Altix.

we have demonstrated a de novo hierarchical QM/ MD simulation framework for the first-principles-based predictive simulation of materials and their validations on high-end parallel computers and geographically distributed grids, with the performance portability across a wide range of parallel platforms.

(i) the EDC framework enables a wide range of high-end atomistic simulations with unprecedented scale and accuracy on high-end parallel platforms, (ii) the EDC parallelization framework achieves high performance tunability and portability on a wide range platforms, and (iii) the framework enables automated hierarchical simulation with automated transition between models, and adaptive resource allocation and migration in a distributed grid environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a hierarchical simulation framework for predictive materials modeling and its efficient implementation on high-end supercomputers.
the development of a new generation of scalable, predictive, and automated materials simulations that are capable of solving complex materials problems that are of interest to the DOE mission.
a systematic development of a de novo hierarchical computational framework for predictive atomistic simulations, and its implementation and optimization on high-end parallel computers and the grid.

our de novo hierarchical simulation has achieved unprecedented scales and performance on high-end parallel computers, while providing a unique capability to perform predictive simulations of materials with unprecedented accuracy.

the de novo hierarchical simulation approach and the framework have been validated at unprecedented scales and have achieved unprecedented performance, and have been demonstrated to be portable and scalable to the largest parallel computers available today.

our framework enables predictive simulation on a petascale computing platform, which will be the key to understanding and predicting the structure, dynamics and function of materials and biological systems at the molecular scale.

we have demonstrated the feasibility of predictive simulations of materials with unprecedented scales, as well as the scalability and portability of the simulation framework.

we are able to achieve a predictive simulation capability that is unprecedented in the history of computational materials science, and that the simulation framework is scalable and portable across high-end computing platforms.

, for the first time, we have demonstrated the predictive capability of the hierarchical simulation framework, and have shown that it can be implemented to run efficiently and effectively on high-end supercomputers and distributed clusters.

high-end computing platforms such a petaflops BlueGene/L and the NSF TIG are an ideal environment for the development of new simulation methods and algorithms for predictive simulations of materials, and for the validation of these methods and algorithms on a large scale.

the hierarchical simulation framework is scalable, portable, and robust, which enables the first-principles-based de novo design of materials and the discovery of new materials with desired properties.
